//: INV-115 constraint map. Keys are either a prohibited code token or "prose:<verbatim governance line>" for a prohibition that carries no grep-able token. Values: {kind,enforcer} for a real, verified enforcer, or {kind:"accepted",rationale} for a judgment-level rule no mechanism can carry. See scripts/check-constraint-scan.mjs --help.

prose:On an error, stop the patch-spiral.rationale: Judgment-level Iron Law: no mechanism can distinguish a diagnosed fix from a guess. Carried by review and by the five-line root-cause writeup CLOSER rule 4 demands after two failed attempts.

prose:**Rule:** Never manually edit `deb.rationale: A hand-loosened baseline is legal JSON every gate accepts; only the reviewed diff on the committed scripts/debt-baseline.json catches it. capture-debt-baseline.mjs --update is the one-way path.

prose:**Rule:** A code-quality rule may.rationale: Tier assignment is an evidence judgment about a metric, not a property any gate can read off a file. Carried at review, plus check-bypass-ceremony.mjs, which forces every advisory site to hold a dated ledger entry.

prose:**Tier-2 (advisory only — do NOT h.rationale: Heading for the Tier-2 list; restates CANON-22's rule above. No mechanism can classify a quality rule's empirical tier, so this stays a review-time judgment.

prose:- Commit directly to `main`.rationale: Enforced out-of-band by GitHub branch protection (required 'CI Required' status, force-push and deletion off), applied by scripts/apply-branch-protection.mjs and re-validated live by scripts/pr-merge-watch.mjs. No local gate can read a remote branch-protection setting.

prose:A failure is never dismissed becau.rationale: Judgment-level Iron Law about attribution, not a checkable property of code: no gate can tell whether a red was inherited or introduced. Carried by review and by the pre-existing-failure clause of CLOSER rule 5.

prose:- **DRY-as-dogma** — duplication _.rationale: Not a prohibition: "never repeat anything" is a quoted dogma the rule REJECTS, inside the Tier-2 advisory list. The extractor sees the bare word never and cannot read the quotation, so this is a marker false positive. Triaged rather than reworded — editing governance prose to fall outside a scanner's grammar makes the doc serve the gate instead of the gate serving the doc, and would let any inconvenient rule be phrased out of the denominator.

prose:layers do not prevent this; only v.rationale: Not a prohibition. "Review layers do not prevent this" is an empirical claim about why verification is required, not a rule anyone can violate; the extractor matches the bare DO NOT and cannot tell a description from a directive. The actual requirement — exercise the changed behaviour before every push — is the sentence above it and is carried by review, since no gate can tell an exercised change from an unexercised one.

prose:The guidance is applied statically.rationale: An architectural absence claim: arbiter performs no runtime model-tier selection. Absence is not locally checkable — proving a feature does not exist anywhere is unbounded — so this is carried at review, backed by the deprecation of the tier-assignment machinery it replaces. The word never here describes arbiter's own design, not a rule imposed on a target project.

prose:- _The RED commit is committable (.rationale: `--no-verify` appears here descriptively, as the thing the pre-commit carve-out exists to make unnecessary for a RED commit — the line introduces no new prohibition. The standing ban on --no-verify is unenforceable by construction in any case: the flag's whole function is to skip the hook that would catch it, so only review and the CI re-run of the gate can see its use.

prose:- No `any` — use `unknown` and nar.rationale: False positive on the recommended ALTERNATIVE, not the prohibition. The rule bans `any`; `unknown` is what it tells you to use instead. The extractor sweeps every backtick token after the No marker to the sentence end, so the remedy is read as a second ban. The real prohibition on this line, `any`, is separately mapped and COVERED by check-no-any.mjs (INV-04).

prose:explanation of origin, never a rea.rationale: Continuation line of the Iron Law already triaged at .claude/CLAUDE.md:113 — the same rule, split across two source lines, so the extractor emits it twice. Judgment-level attribution prose: no gate can tell whether a red was inherited or introduced. Carried by review and by the pre-existing-failure clause of CLOSER rule 5.

prose:- _Baseline decay (#2418):_ `scrip.rationale: False positive on the ENFORCING flags, not a prohibition. The line's rule is that the fail-closed baseline may only shrink; the extractor matches the bare word never and sweeps the backticked tokens that follow, but `--update-baseline` and `--owner` are the mechanisms that IMPOSE that rule (regeneration preserves rows verbatim; grandfathering a newly-violating file requires an owner), not symbols anyone is banned from using. Same shape as the `unknown` case on AGENTS.md:456 — the remedy a rule recommends read as a second ban. The rule itself is carried by scripts/check-fail-closed-audit.mjs, which fails on an expired row, a window past 90 days, and a row whose file no longer violates.
